 The Netherlands and Greece meet in the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 on Friday, 13 November, at 19:45 GMT . The match takes place at the Johan Cruijff ArenA in Amsterdam, with both nations looking to strengthen their position at the top of League A, Group 2.
 Both teams remain unbeaten after four matches, collecting eight points each. Their previous encounter ended in a 2-2 draw in October, setting up another competitive meeting between two sides with ambitions of reaching the quarter-finals.

 Netherlands vs. Greece - Head-to-head record
 The Netherlands have dominated this fixture historically, recording nine victories, one draw and one defeat in 11 meetings before their October 2026 encounter.
 Their recent competitive meetings have also favoured the Dutch. The Netherlands defeated Greece 3-0 at home in September 2023 before securing a narrow 1-0 away victory the following month during European Championship qualifying.
 However, Greece proved more difficult to overcome when the teams met on 1 October 2026. The match finished 2-2, with Greece demonstrating their ability to compete against a Dutch side containing several established European stars.
 That result ended a run of Dutch victories in this fixture and highlighted Greece’s recent improvement. Nevertheless, the Netherlands’ strong historical record and home advantage make them the favourites heading into Friday’s encounter.

 Netherlands - Looking to take control of Group 2
 The Netherlands enter this fixture level on points with Greece at the top of their Nations League group . With Germany also competing for qualification, a home victory would be particularly valuable.
 Recent form
 The Netherlands have enjoyed an unbeaten start to their Nations League campaign , recording two victories and two draws from four matches.
 They opened with a 1-1 draw against Germany before securing a 2-1 away victory over Serbia. A 2-2 draw against Greece followed, before the Dutch defeated Serbia 2-1 again in October.
 Their attacking performances have been consistent, with seven goals scored across four matches. However, they have also conceded five, demonstrating that their defensive organisation remains an area for improvement.
 The Netherlands have scored in each of their four Nations League matches, but have yet to keep a clean sheet. Their ability to create chances has helped compensate for defensive vulnerabilities, particularly against opponents willing to attack.
 Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey are unavailable for this international window, while Nathan Aké is also sidelined. These absences create additional selection challenges, particularly in central defence.
 Despite those setbacks, the Netherlands possess considerable attacking quality. Cody Gakpo, Tijjani Reijnders, and Donyell Malen provide different attacking options, while their midfield is capable of controlling possession for extended periods.

 Greece - Looking to extend their unbeaten run
 Greece arrive in Amsterdam level on points with the Netherlands and unbeaten in the Nations League. Ivan Jovanović’s side have demonstrated their ability to compete against strong opposition, making them dangerous visitors.
 Recent form
 Greece have collected eight points from their opening four Nations League matches, recording two victories and two draws.
 They began with a 2-1 away victory against Serbia before defeating Germany 1-0. Their next two matches ended in draws, including the entertaining 2-2 encounter against the Netherlands and a goalless draw with Germany.
 Greece have scored five goals and conceded three across those four matches. Their defensive record is better than the Netherlands’, with two clean sheets demonstrating their ability to frustrate stronger opponents.
 Their attacking threat comes from players such as Vangelis Pavlidis and Fotis Ioannidis , while Konstantinos Karetsas provides creativity between midfield and attack.
 However, Greece face selection challenges. Christos Zafeiris and Manolis Saliakas are suspended, while Giannis Konstantelias and Dimitrios Pelkas are unavailable through injury.
 The visitors will need another disciplined performance to leave Amsterdam with a positive result. Their ability to absorb pressure and exploit counterattacking opportunities will be particularly important against a Dutch side that prefers to dominate possession.

 Predictions for Netherlands vs. Greece - Netherlands tipped for victory
 The Netherlands enter this fixture with home advantage and a strong historical record against Greece . Their attacking quality makes them favourites, although Greece’s unbeaten Nations League campaign suggests another competitive encounter.
 The Dutch have scored in every group match but have also conceded in all four. That makes over 2.5 goals and a decisive result an interesting option, particularly after the teams shared four goals in October.
 Greece have demonstrated defensive resilience against Germany, but the Netherlands’ movement and attacking variety should create opportunities. A match featuring over 3.5 goals and a winner is another option for those expecting an open contest.
 Our main prediction is for the Netherlands to win with a -0.5 Asian Handicap. Playing in Amsterdam gives the Dutch an advantage, and their attacking strength could prove decisive against a Greece side missing two suspended players.
